open_points.subject: M05 publisher
open_points.text: the two forms of a pointer's publisher (M13, M14)
open_points.question: What named closed type contains PrincipalPublisher and ImportPublisher, and what discriminator distinguishes them?
options: Declare a named discriminated union with M13 and M14 as its variants
Make M05 carry separate optional fields for the two forms
Treat publisher as an untyped value interpreted from context
open_points.default_guess: Declare a named discriminated union with explicit principal and import variants.

witness.initial: A store contains one imported pointer and one pointer published later by the owner.
events: Registry imports the first pointer and records M14.
The owner publishes the second pointer and Registry records M13.
A service reads both pointer histories.
outcomes: The reader receives one typed publisher field whose discriminator selects M13 or M14.
The reader receives an ad hoc shape or optional fields chosen by the contract writer.

open_points.subject: M09 audit subject
open_points.text: the five forms of an audit entry's subject (M15–M19)
open_points.question: What named closed type contains M15–M19, and what discriminator distinguishes its five variants?
options: Declare a named discriminated union with M15–M19 as variants
Put several optional subject fields directly on M09
Infer the subject form from the audit action
open_points.default_guess: Declare a named discriminated union with an explicit discriminator.

open_points.subject: M13 — PrincipalPublisher
open_points.text: Facts: the principal (M07).
open_points.question: When Kernel publishes for an agent, does M13 also carry the agent session required by R0-92, or is that session already a fact of M07?
options: The session is a fact inside M07
M13 has a separate session fact when Kernel publishes
M05, rather than M13, carries the session separately
open_points.default_guess: Make the Kernel principal variant of M07 carry the session identity.

witness.initial: Two registered agent sessions use the same Cabinet Kernel principal and can publish to the same granted project.
events: Kernel publishes a pointer for session A.
Kernel publishes another pointer for session B.
The owner examines the publishers to follow R0-92's link.
outcomes: The publishers identify sessions A and B separately.
Both publishers contain only the same Kernel principal and cannot identify the publishing session.
witness.observer: The owner tracing a pointer to the agent session

open_points.subject: M20 — PendingConfirmation
open_points.text: Facts: its one-time value;
open_points.question: Is the one-time value the same fact as M11's “confirmation id”, or are the value and confirmation id two distinct facts?
options: They are the same fact
They are two distinct facts
M20 carries the value while another model carries the confirmation id
open_points.default_guess: Treat them as the same per-confirmation identifier.

open_points.subject: M20 — PendingConfirmation
open_points.text: the confirmed action; its target, when the action has one; the revision or access version the step showed, when it showed one; the inputs it is bound to, by their digest;
open_points.question: For each confirmation-producing product action, which target, version and input-digest facts must M20 contain?
options: Declare a closed variant per confirmation action with its applicable facts
Use one product with optional target, revision, access version and digest facts
Store only a single opaque binding digest for every action
open_points.default_guess: Declare closed action-specific variants so inapplicable facts cannot be guessed.

witness.initial: The owner can archive a project, erase a project, or accept an import, all with confirmation.
events: Registry later shows an import confirmation.
outcomes: Each pending value has a defined action-specific target, version and input binding.
Implementers independently choose whether targets and versions are absent, generic or encoded into one digest.
witness.observer: Registry when checking the submitted confirmation

open_points.subject: M21 — UploadedFile
open_points.text: its upload number within the session, so that an upload of the same bytes is still another upload
open_points.question: Who assigns the upload number, when is it assigned, and from what state is it derived?
options: Registry assigns the next number in the owner session on every accepted upload
The owner interface supplies the number
The number is derived from the file digest or another file fact
open_points.default_guess: Registry assigns a monotonically increasing session-local number when it accepts an upload.

witness.initial: An owner session has no uploaded file.
events: The owner uploads the identical bytes X again.
Registry shows a confirmation for the second upload.
outcomes: Registry assigns distinct session-local upload numbers to the two uploads.
The repeated bytes retain the same number or receive a caller-selected number.
witness.observer: Registry checking which upload the confirmation binds

open_points.subject: M21 — UploadedFile
open_points.text: The owner's upload in the owner interface (A16 rule 1).
open_points.question: Which product action creates or replaces M21: a separate upload action, the import action itself, or the action that displays import confirmation?
options: A separate owner upload action creates or replaces M21
Starting the import creates or replaces M21
Displaying the confirmation creates or replaces M21
open_points.default_guess: Use a separate authenticated owner upload action that replaces the session's current M21.

open_points.subject: M23 — ServiceRight
open_points.text: A row of the service rights table: one operation one service's token may call (State 2 A09 rule 3).
open_points.question: What is the complete set of service-operation rows in SERVICE_RIGHTS?
options: Enumerate every allowed service-operation pair in State 1
Derive rows from State 0 actor prose
Leave the provider or contract writer to choose the rows
open_points.default_guess: Enumerate every allowed service-operation pair explicitly before handoff.

witness.initial: Cabinet Kernel and PresuPro each possess a service token.
events: Each service calls an operation not explicitly assigned to it in the supplied text.
outcomes: The operation is allowed because one implementer inferred a row from broad actor prose.
The operation is refused because another implementer omitted that inferred row.

open_points.subject: M24 — ServiceHighestClass
open_points.text: One row per service.
open_points.question: Which services have rows, and what exact highest disclosure class is assigned to each?
options: Enumerate every service and its highest class in State 1
Infer the rows from descriptions of current callers
Let deployment data choose the rows
open_points.default_guess: Enumerate PresuPro, Client Portal, Cabinet and Cabinet Kernel explicitly with their decided highest classes.

open_points.subject: M25 — PersonalDataField
open_points.text: Facts: the answer's name; the field's name.
open_points.question: What is the complete set of answer-and-field pairs classified as personal_data?
options: Enumerate every pair in State 1
Classify whole answers instead of individual fields
Let contract authors infer pairs from prose
open_points.default_guess: Enumerate every personal-data output field explicitly in State 1.

witness.initial: A service token permits business_confidential output but not personal_data.
events: The service requests an answer containing a field whose classification is not enumerated.
outcomes: The inferred row exists and Registry refuses or filters the answer.
The row is absent and Registry returns the field.
witness.observer: The calling service and the recipient of the field

open_points.subject: M27 — OwnerActionRoute
open_points.text: whether it touches an uploaded file (A16 rule 2).
open_points.question: For which owner actions is “touches an uploaded file” true, and does touching mean creating, replacing, reading, accepting or dropping M21?
options: Enumerate the actions and their precise M21 effect
Use one boolean for all forms of access without distinguishing effects
Infer the value and effect from each route handler
open_points.default_guess: Enumerate upload as create/replace and import acceptance as read/drop, with all other actions false.

open_points.subject: M28 — OwnerAuditAction
open_points.text: which audit action (M09, R0-58) an accepted owner action writes — for a customer mark, by its transition; for a project's erasure, by its kind
open_points.question: What is the complete mapping from accepted owner actions, customer transitions and project-erasure kinds to audit actions, including which accepted actions write no audit entry?
options: Enumerate every mapping row and explicit no-entry case
Infer audit actions from the product action names
Let each handler choose whether and what to audit
open_points.default_guess: Enumerate all significant-change mappings and explicitly exclude the actions R0-92 says are not audited.

witness.initial: The owner accepts a customer transition and a project erasure.
events: The owner lifts a customer restriction.
The owner deletes an archived project whole.
The owner reads the audit log.
outcomes: Both handlers use an explicit table and write the prescribed audit actions.
Each handler infers a different action name or one omits its entry because the table has no declared rows.
witness.observer: The owner reading the audit log

open_points.subject: Status; M22–M28
open_points.text:
Reopened on 2026-11-25: the assembled specification held sixteen runtime
models with no record here (the identity closure's `missing_state1_model`).
None adds a concept: each is a value a model above already names, or a row of
a table of the release, and each now has its record — the two forms of a
pointer's publisher (M13, M14), the five forms of an audit entry's subject
(M15–M19), the owner session's pending confirmation and uploaded file (M20,
M21; the upload number, which State 6 carried on the owner's word of
2026-11-24, is now a fact of M11), and the rows of the data provider's seven
tables (M22–M28).
open_points.rule: Большие структурные доменные справочники и catalog/mapping tables тоже живут в `models`, если это domain taxonomy или upstream/downstream contract. Справочник, который читает генерируемый код, доставляет константа поставщика данных (§15.3.1): запись `models` с таким `kind` до кода не доходит.
open_points.question: The passage must classify the seven release tables as catalog/mapping/vocabulary spec data delivered by provider constants, rather than calling their rows runtime models, or state why any genuine runtime DTO is a separate contract model.

open_points.subject: M11 — OwnerSession
open_points.text:
at most one uploaded import
file — its bytes, their digest and its upload number within the session
(owner, 2026-11-24) — replaced by the next upload and dropped when the import
is accepted.
open_points.question: The added uploaded-file facts must become declared fields with types.

open_points.subject: M13 — PrincipalPublisher
open_points.text: Facts: the principal (M07).
open_points.question: The principal fact must become a declared field with its type.

open_points.subject: M14 — ImportPublisher
open_points.text: Facts: the digest of the accepted file (M10).
open_points.question: The accepted-file digest must become a declared field with its type.

open_points.subject: M15 — ProjectSubject
open_points.text: Facts: the project's identity (M01).
open_points.question: The project identity must become a declared field with its type.

open_points.subject: M16 — CustomerSubject
open_points.text: Facts: the customer's identity (M04).
open_points.question: The customer identity must become a declared field with its type.

open_points.subject: M17 — SessionProjectSubject
open_points.text: Facts: the session's identity (M06); the project's identity (M01).
open_points.question: Both identities must become declared fields with types.

open_points.subject: M18 — ImportSubject
open_points.text: Facts: the digest of the accepted file (M10).
open_points.question: The accepted-file digest must become a declared field with its type.

open_points.subject: M20 — PendingConfirmation
open_points.text:
Facts: its one-time value; the confirmed action; its target, when the action
has one; the revision or access version the step showed, when it showed one;
the inputs it is bound to, by their digest; and when it was shown, as the
session's monotonic reading (A13), since its limits are measured on that
clock.
open_points.question: Every pending-confirmation fact must become a declared field with a type and any default or optionality stated as required.

open_points.subject: M21 — UploadedFile
open_points.text:
Facts: its bytes, as uploaded; their digest, by which the mapping names the
file (A16 rule 2); and its upload number within the session, so that an upload
of the same bytes is still another upload and a confirmation step binds the
upload it showed (owner, 2026-11-24; `60_contracts.md`).
open_points.question: Bytes, digest and upload number must become declared fields with types.

open_points.subject: M22 — ArtifactTypeOwner
open_points.text: Facts: the artifact type; its owner service.
open_points.question: Both row facts must become declared fields with types in the appropriate catalog model.

open_points.subject: M23 — ServiceRight
open_points.text: Facts: the service; the operation.
open_points.question: Service and operation must become declared fields with types in the appropriate mapping model.

open_points.subject: M24 — ServiceHighestClass
open_points.text: Facts: the service; its highest class.
open_points.question: Service and highest class must become declared fields with types in the appropriate mapping model.

open_points.subject: M25 — PersonalDataField
open_points.text: Facts: the answer's name; the field's name.
open_points.question: Answer name and field name must become declared fields with types in the appropriate mapping model.

open_points.subject: M26 — RefusalHttpStatus
open_points.text: Facts: the refusal code; its HTTP status.
open_points.question: Refusal code and HTTP status must become declared fields with types in the appropriate mapping model.

open_points.subject: M27 — OwnerActionRoute
open_points.text:
Facts: the owner action; its method; its path; whether it is a change;
whether it touches an uploaded file.
open_points.question: Every owner-action row fact must become a declared field with a type in the appropriate mapping model.

open_points.subject: M28 — OwnerAuditAction
open_points.text:
Facts: the owner action; the customer mark's transition, where the action has
one; the project erasure's kind, where the action has one; the audit action it
writes.
open_points.question: Every owner-audit row fact must become a declared field with a type, with defaults or optionality stated for the conditional facts.
